title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: G is an algebraic group over Q. Rep(G) is meant as a candidate motivic Galois category. S = Res_{C/R} G_m and U = ker(Norm: S -> G_{m,R}). Real Hodge pre-structures on the fibre functor that are compatible with the Q-structure and functorial in V are the same thing as a homomorphism h: S -> G_R; on this page Grothendieck calls it j. A central homomorphism i: G_m -> G, the weight cocharacter, gives a grading of the fibre functor.

This page:
(a) Compatibility of the Hodge bigrading with the weight grading (V^n_C = sum over p+q=n of V^{p,q}) is j restricted to G_{m,R} equals i_R. From now on i is fixed.
The Tate object Q(1) is an invertible object of Rep(G). Up to isomorphism it is a character eps: G -> G_m.
Q(1) has Hodge bidegree (1,1) if and only if eps(j(lambda)) = lambda^2 for real lambda and eps(j(u)) = 1 for u in U. Equivalently, condition (b): eps o j = Norm: S -> G_{m,R}. The two descriptions agree because S = G_{m,R}·U with intersection mu_2, and (-1)^2 = 1.
Grothendieck then fixes (i, eps) with eps o i = (lambda -> lambda^2) and restricts to the j satisfying (a) and (b). In modern terms (G, i, eps) is a Tate triple (Deligne–Milne 1982, §5; Saavedra Rivano 1972, Ch. V), with h: S -> G_R a Hodge cocharacter compatible with it.
He then asks: for V in Rep(G) of weight p, which G-equivariant forms phi: V x V -> Q(-p) are polarizations of the associated Hodge structure? Answer (**): phi_R(x, Cy) is symmetric and positive definite on V_R, where C = h(sqrt(-1)) is the Weil operator. C acts by i^{p-q} on V^{p,q}, since lambda^p·conj(lambda)^q evaluated at lambda = i gives i^{p-q}.
The next page continues: phi is (-1)^n-symmetric, and G is isomorphic to G' x_{mu_2} G_m with G' = ker eps and eta = i(-1). The theorem there states that the following are equivalent: polarizability of all of Rep(G); polarizability of a faithful family; the same over R. Each implies that the centralizer of h(i) in G'^0_R is maximal compact, i.e. ad h(i) is a Cartan involution.
The page thus serves a project: making the motivic Galois group, the Hodge realization (Mumford–Tate type data) and polarizations (the standard conjectures and positivity) into one group-theoretic package.
errors: Sign or normalization inconsistency. Here Q(1) has bidegree (1,1), weight 2, and eps o i = lambda^2. A pairing V x V -> target with V of weight p then needs a target of weight 2p, i.e. Q(p) in this convention, but Grothendieck writes Q(-p) (and Q(-n) on the next page). Either Q(1) is being used for the Lefschetz object H^2(P^1), which is Q(-1) in the modern convention where Q(1) has bidegree (-1,-1), or the target should be Q(p). This is harmless but should be flagged.

Minor gap: (**) is stated as the definition of polarization without first imposing (-1)^p-symmetry of phi. It is only remarked on the next page that symmetry of phi(x, Cy) forces phi to be alternating or symmetric according to the parity of the weight. This is consistent but left implicit.

ideas.what: Polarization of a representation as a G-equivariant pairing V x V -> Q(-p) with phi(x, Cy) symmetric positive definite, C = h(i)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Riemann polarization via the Weil operator; polarization of a Tannakian category
ideas.where_published: Deligne, Hodge II / Shimura; Saavedra Ch. V

missed.claim: Circa 1965 Grothendieck already uses the Deligne torus S, the Hodge cocharacter h: S -> G_R, and a Tate character eps with eps o w = squaring (a Tate triple) to describe Hodge realizations of a motivic Galois group. On the next page this leads to a theorem tying polarizability of Rep(G) to h(i) inducing a Cartan involution (centralizer of h(i) maximal compact). These are usually credited to Deligne (1971–79) and Saavedra/Deligne–Milne (1972/82). Saavedra's debt to Grothendieck is known in general; this explicit early formulation is not documented.
missed.quote: ε j = Norme : S → G_m R ... φ_R(x, Cy) forme symétrique, définie positive sur V_R × V_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it places the S-formalism and the Tate-triple / polarization package in Grothendieck's motivic Galois program before Deligne's Shimura-variety axioms. The dating is uncertain, since the notes are s.d. and only the letter is dated 1965.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (Deligne torus, Tate triples, polarizations via the Weil operator). Seeing it already packaged around 1965 in Grothendieck's hand, before Deligne and Saavedra, is a notable but unsurprising-in-spirit historical detail, given that Saavedra's thesis is known to derive from Grothendieck's program.
